Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:40: Let us return to the discourse. He says further there, in the Tikkunim (66a): "'set me as a seal' - this is the soul, which is engraved on the Throne; when it is aroused below in prayer, the Throne is aroused above. 'As a seal' - this is ruach, which is the image of the letter Shin engraved among the angels; when it is aroused below in prayer, the angels are aroused with it above. 'Upon your arm' - this is nefesh, which is engraved in the four directions of the world; when it is aroused below in prayer, the four directions of the world are aroused with it. The neshamah is the seal, the ruach is the shape of the letters engraved in the seal, the nefesh is the imprint of the letters in the seal, which are marked in a person's features like the imprint of a seal on a document, and by that imprint of the nefesh, the countenance is recognized in a person's body - from what place it comes" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:41: It remains for us to explain in this chapter the matter of the blemish to the Shechinah with which we began. It says in the Tikkunim (52a) - his words: "Another explanation: (Genesis 27:4) 'and make me savory food such as I love' - from the positive commandments, 'and not such as I hate' - from the negative commandments. The negative commandments depend upon the fear that is Yirah, and they serve to distance Satan from them, so that he not draw near to the Throne, which is the heart, to demand judgments upon the holy limbs, who are Israel, and to bring the Shechinah among them" - so far. The meaning is that the negative commandments are all fences preventing Samael from entering within holiness to arouse judgments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:42: It is further explained in the Tikkunim (55a) - his words, on the matter of the level of "two savory dishes": what is "two savory dishes"? Rather, after he ascends to his level, he will say to Israel, "and make me savory food such as I love" - from the positive commandments, comprised within the Heh of Abraham, comprising two hundred and forty-eight commandments, through which the Heh draws near to the Vav, and this offering is the drawing near of the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Shechinah. The positive commandments are given from the right, the negative commandments from the left, and these are the "two savory dishes"; the positive commandments are the food of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the negative commandments are food for Samael, for whoever transgresses them. This is what Esau brought near to Isaac, saying to him (Genesis 27:31) "let my father arise and eat of his son's venison," and it is on their account that Samael would draw near to the left, to give the Holy One, blessed be He, a taste of the sins of their children, which are bitter foods, on account of which it is said (Malachi 1:3) "but Esau I hated"" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:43: Here it is explained that the positive commandments are the food of the Holy One, blessed be He, because every mitzvah brings about union and draws a spiritual, holy flow from the side of kindness; and whoever transgresses a negative commandment breaches the fence and causes Samael to enter above and arouse the attribute of judgment, from the side of Gevurah, so that his portion be bestowed upon him. And once judgment is bestowed through the Shechinah, she tastes of it - this is [the meaning of] "to give the Holy One, blessed be He, a taste of the sins of their children, which are bitter foods" - the meaning being that they cause the bitterness of judgment to be aroused from the left side, and the secret of this bitterness is explained by my teacher, peace be upon him, and the matter of tasting this bitterness is explained (see Pardes, Gate of the Soul, chapter 11).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:44: Further, Rashbi explains (Acharei 74a) - his words: "Rabbi Yehudah said: when the righteous increase in the world, Knesset Yisrael ascends with good scents and is blessed by the Holy King, and her countenance shines; but when the wicked increase in the world, as it were, Knesset Yisrael does not ascend with good scents and is given a taste from the other, bitter side, and then it is written (Lamentations 2:1) 'He has cast down from heaven to earth,' etc., and her countenance is darkened. Rabbi Yosi said: when the righteous increase in the world, it is written (Song of Songs 2:6) 'his left hand is under my head and his right hand embraces me'; and when the wicked increase in the world, it is written (Lamentations 2:3) 'He has drawn back His right hand.' Rabbi Chizkiyah said, this is derived from here (Proverbs 16:28) 'and a talebearer separates close friends' - meaning, he separates the King from the Matronita - this is [the meaning of] (Leviticus 18:7) 'the nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover.'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:45: Here it is explained how great the blemish is, in various aspects - whether concerning the tasting of bitterness that reaches the Shechinah, and her countenance becoming dark; and the reason her countenance darkens is because "a foolish son is the grief of his mother" (Proverbs 10:1), as is further explained there below, that he ought to have been disciplined, as it is said (Proverbs 31:1) "the words of Lemuel king, the burden with which his mother instructed him," and it says that the King never punishes a person Himself, but leaves everything in the hand of the Matronita to govern the palace and to punish the son and lead him in the true path before the King; and when the son conducts himself properly, he is called "a wise son makes a father glad" - "father" unqualified, referring to the One above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:46: It says there that when Solomon the king composed the Song of Songs, what great joy was made above, and when he built the Temple, a supernal union was made above, and all the worlds were in joy and radiance; and it says, why all this? Because it is written "with which his mother instructed him," for she led him to the King's desire.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:47: It says: and when this person, as I have said, is not led to the King's will, then it is nakedness of everything, nakedness on all sides, for the King separates from the Matronita and the Matronita is distanced from His palace - so far. This is the aspect of "a talebearer separates close friends" - that the blemish reaches even the King, being separated from His palace, and this is "the nakedness of your father," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:48: This is likewise explained in the portion of Vayikra (Zohar 16b) - his words: "Another explanation: (Proverbs 16:28) 'a perverse man sends forth strife [madon]' - what is 'sends forth'? He sends it to those saplings, madon - who draw from the side of judgment [din]. 'And a talebearer separates close friends' - as we have said, the wicked cause a blemish above, separating - the [divine] union is not found, separating the Matronita from the King and the King from the Matronita, and therefore it is not called 'one' - for 'one' is called only when they are in a single union. Woe to those wicked who cause separation above; happy are the righteous who maintain the union above" - so far. This is a second aspect concerning the blemish reaching Tiferet, that all six directions, called "saplings," all draw from judgment, as it says "sends forth strife."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:49: Further, concerning the blemish reaching the Shechinah, is what Rashbi says (Bereishit 22a): the matter of "a foolish son is the grief of his mother" is because through her the creation of man came about from the start - his being composed of good and evil - and therefore it is she who bears the shame from her son.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:50: Further, it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Korach 178b) - his words: "the Shechinah - whoever does an act of kindness with her, there is no measure to his reward, and whoever sins against her, there is no measure to his punishment" - so far. And further, in Ra'aya Meheimna, portion of Tzav (28b), on the verse (Leviticus 6:6) "a perpetual fire shall be kept burning on the altar" - concerning the matter that a transgression does not extinguish Torah, but a transgression does extinguish a mitzvah, it says: whoever commits a transgression that extinguishes a mitzvah, which is a candle, likewise extinguishes his own candle, of which it is said (Proverbs 20:27) "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man" - it is extinguished from his own body, so that the body remains in darkness; so too, whoever removes the Shechinah from her place causes an extinguishing for the whole world and darkness for that place, and darkness is transgression - "and a maidservant that supplants her mistress" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:51: The reason is as was explained above in the passage we quoted from the Tikkunim, that the Shechinah is comprised of all the supernal sefirot, all the expressions of being, all the names, all the souls, the Throne, the angels, etc. - everything is depicted in her. We find, then, that when a person betters his deeds with her, he does an act of kindness with all the worlds comprised within her, all of which then shine, and the branches of the sefirah planted within her arouse their supernal roots in the masculine, so that they arouse the drawing down of mercy and flow even from the very highest, from the Cause of everything, blessed be He - and therefore there is no measure to his reward. And when, God forbid, he blemishes, the blemish reaches all the realities within her, which all turn to judgment, causing the extinguishing of the light for all the worlds and darkness to rule - the maidservant in place of her mistress - and therefore there is no measure to his punishment. May God, in His mercy, grant us the merit of being among those who do acts of kindness with her, Amen.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:1: This chapter will explain the remaining aspects of the blemish. There is also a blemish to Tiferet, explained in the Zohar (Yitro 85b) - his words: "we learn that all the commandments of the Torah are unified in the body of the King - some in the King's head, some in His body, some in the King's hands, and some in His feet, and there is nothing that goes outside the body of the King."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:2: This same wording is quoted in the Tikkunim (131a): "and therefore, whoever transgresses the commandments of the Torah is as though he transgressed against the body of the King, as it is written (Isaiah 66:24) 'and they shall go out and see the corpses of the men who transgressed against Me' - against Me, literally. Woe to the wicked who transgress the words of the Torah and do not know what they are doing, for Rabbi Shimon said: the very place against which he sinned, that very place reveals his sin. And Rabbi Shimon said: the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself reveals the sin - if one sins against the Holy One, blessed be He, the Holy One, blessed be He, reveals his sin, as it is written (Job 20:27) 'the heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him' - 'the heavens shall reveal his iniquity' refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, 'and the earth shall rise up against him' refers to the Holy One, blessed be He [i.e., both refer to Him in different aspects]. It is taught: the heavens reveal a person's sin, and at the time it is revealed, the earth executes judgment upon the person, as it is written 'and the earth shall rise up against him,' to execute judgment upon him" - so far. His words are self-explanatory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:3: We draw from the totality of his words one aspect of fear: one must fear sinning, for although the King currently shows him a cheerful face and does not immediately show anger, it is nonetheless the King's way to conceal judgment within Himself, and afterward exact full payment - as is explained in the portion of Beshalach (51b), regarding the reason the word "vayet" ["and he stretched out," Exodus 14:21] is written entirely straight, and not half straight and half inverted, corresponding to Tiferet as a whole; and they answer that it is the King's way to conceal judgment - the fool, seeing the King's cheerful face, sins and does not guard against His judgment, but the wise one says, although the King's face is cheerful, He keeps judgment concealed within Himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:4: This is [the meaning of] "the heavens shall reveal his iniquity" - for they will reveal in the future what was concealed. "And the earth shall rise up against him" - for she is the one who avenges the vengeance of the covenant, and there are two vengeances: one for what he blemished in her, and one corresponding to what he blemished in Him [Tiferet], as with "a talebearer separates close friends," which was explained. The Mother at first is silent, even though he has blemished, because "a foolish son is the grief of his mother," until the Father comes and reveals the blemish in the limb where he blemished, and then she rises up against him to discipline him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:5: Along these lines, Rashbi explains (Vayikra 23b), on the verse "and the earth shall rise up against him" - his words: "Rabbi Yehudah opened, (Leviticus 4:23) 'or his sin, which he has sinned, is made known to him' - 'made known to him' from whose side? It should say 'or he knows his sin'; what is 'made known to him'? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, commands Knesset Yisrael to make known to the person that sin which he has sinned - and by what does He make it known to him? By her judgments, along the lines of 'the heavens shall reveal his iniquity and the earth shall rise up against him.' 'Made known to him' - as He commanded another [passage], for we learn, when a person sins before the Holy One, blessed be He, and does not pay attention to his sin to return in repentance before his Master, but casts it behind his back, his very soul ascends and testifies before the Holy One, blessed be He; then the King commands Knesset Yisrael and says, 'or his sin, which he has sinned, is made known to him' - He stretches judgment over him and makes his sin known to him, along the lines of (Ezekiel 16:2) 'make known to Jerusalem her abominations.' After judgment reaches him, then his spirit is aroused to return in repentance before his Master and to submit to bringing an offering - for whoever is coarse of heart sins and forgets his sins and does not pay attention to it, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is ready against him and commands that this sin be made known to him so that it not be forgotten by him" - so far. His intent is that the attribute "O" [Aleph-Vav, numerically seven] makes a person's sin known to him, and "made known" is a command from the Holy One, blessed be He, to her, to make the sin known to the person.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:6: Along these lines it is explained in the Zohar (Chukat 180b) that one must fear the judgment that is in the Shechinah - that at first her countenance shines upon a person, and afterward she strikes and kills. It says there that the Shechinah is called "the bent Nun," and it says afterward, why is she called this? Rather, as it is said (Leviticus 25:17) "do not wrong [lo tonu] one another" - for now her countenance shines and she does a "wrong" [ona'ah] to human beings, and afterward she strikes like a serpent and destroys and kills, and says, "I have not done iniquity [avel]" - so far. Concerning this Solomon the king, peace be upon him, commanded (Proverbs 20:2) "the king's terror is like the roar of a young lion; he who provokes him to anger sins against his own soul" - as though saying, he becomes liable with his own soul, as they say in the Mishnah (Avot 3:4), "he becomes liable with his own soul" - and concerning this he also said (ibid. 24:21) "fear the Lord, my son, and the king."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:7: Further, there (Yitro 85b) it says: when the Mother sits upon her children, all the worlds are in joy and completeness; when the Mother is removed, they are all removed from their place; and it is written (Deuteronomy 22:6) "do not take the mother with the young," and we learn: a person should not commit sins below, so as to cause the Mother to be removed from over her children - so far. Here it is explained that the blemish reaches even to the removal of the Mother from over the children, who are the six directions.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:8: Further, it is explained in the Tikkunim (8a) that sometimes the blemish reaches all the letters of YHVH - his words: "and the secret of the matter is that they can destroy the letters of His Name, as it is said (Exodus 19:21) 'lest they break through to the Lord [YHVH]'; and because they destroy them through their sins, one must rebuild them through prayer" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:9: Further, concerning the magnitude of the blemish, it is further explained in the Tikkunim (17a), in the words of Elijah - their words: "and since You are within, whoever separates one from its fellow among these ten [sefirot] is considered as though he separated within You" - so far. My teacher, peace be upon him, explains that this is like the parable of one who tears the King's garments off the King - understand this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:10: Further, there is a blemish to the Throne, explained in the Tikkunim (3b) - their words: "of the Shechinah it is said (Song of Songs 1:6) 'do not look at me, for I am swarthy,' because she is in exile and her Throne is blemished by the sins of Israel, for the souls of Israel are there; and therefore happy is one who repairs her Throne through his prayers and his commandments, for after the Throne is blemished because of them, the Name YHVH departs from there, since He does not rest in a blemished place, as it is said (Leviticus 21:18) 'any who has a defect shall not draw near' - so too He does not rest in a blemished soul; happy is one who completes his soul so that the Name YHVH rests within it and makes it a Throne for Him" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:11: We find, then, that a person can blemish the Throne in three aspects. First, the Shechinah, since her Throne is blemished, suffers, because she is a soul clothed within the Throne - and just as pain reaches a soul when the body is blemished, struck, and afflicted on account of sins, so does the Shechinah, who is clothed within the Throne, suffer from the blemishes to the Throne. And it explains that the blemish reaches the Throne because of the root of the souls that are in the Throne - this is [the meaning of] "the souls of Israel are there" - and when they blemish below, they blemish the Throne above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:12: From this comes a second aspect of blemish: that the souls will not arouse "female waters" for the Shechinah once they are blemished in the Throne, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:13: Third: that Tiferet, who is YHVH, who is "Adam" sitting upon the Throne, withdraws entirely - this is "and the Name YHVH departs from there," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:14: Further, Rashbi explains (Beha'alotcha 149b) that in the Throne all sins are depicted and written - his words: "at the time judgment hangs over the world and judgments prevail, and the Holy One, blessed be He, sits on the Throne of Judgment to judge the world upon that Throne - how many markings are marked upon it, how many hidden documents are stored within it, within the King's treasury! All the books that are opened there are stored there, and therefore not a single word is forgotten by the King. And this Throne is not established and does not rest except in the seventh month, which is the day of judgment, the day on which all the world's inhabitants are recorded, all passing before that Throne" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:15: Further, concerning the blemish reaching the world of angels, one must fear, for there are seven angels called "the eyes of the Lord roaming about," who testify to every blemish depicted within them, and go and testify before the seventy Sanhedrin - this is explained in the Zohar (Mishpatim 107a) - his words: "it is written (II Chronicles 16:9) 'for the eyes of the Lord roam through all the earth' - these are feminine; and it is written (Zechariah 4:10) 'these are the eyes of the Lord, they roam about' - these are masculine, and they are already known. David said (Psalms 51:6) 'and I have done evil in Your eyes' - it should say 'before Your eyes'; rather, what is 'in Your eyes'? David said: in that place where I sinned, Your eyes were there, for I knew that Your eyes were ready and standing before me, yet I did not consider them - so here is the sin I sinned, in the very place where Your eyes were."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:16: This is likewise explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Emor 99a): the appointed guardian comes and demands judgment for all the deeds of the world's inhabitants, each one according to his ways and according to what he did, and witnesses come and testify concerning all the deeds of the world's inhabitants - these are "the eyes of the Lord" that roam through the whole world; and there are countless "eyes of the Lord" that go about and roam through the whole world and see all the deeds of the world's inhabitants. Woe to those who do not heed or pay attention to their deeds, for the King's witnesses stand and go alongside them, watching; and this appointed guardian stands before the King and demands judgment - so-and-so did such a deed, so-and-so did this - and here are the witnesses.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:17: Further, of this kind is that one causes the impure Samael to enter among the world of the holy angels to teach accusation - will they not say, who caused this reeking, impure one to enter among us? Surely he will be punished.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:18: Further, concerning the blemish pertaining to the angels, it is explained in the Sabba (Mishpatim 106b), on the verse (Isaiah 57:18) "and I will restore comforts to him and to his mourners" - it says that the two angels who always accompany a person to guard him, of whom it is said (Psalms 91:11) "for He shall command His angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways," when a person sins, they separate from him and stand mourning over him because of his sin; and when he repents - as it is said, "I have seen his ways, and will heal him; and I will lead him and restore comforts to him" - first, because he repented and comforted himself over what had passed, and afterward "and to his mourners" - who are the angels who had been standing in mourning over him. Therefore it is fitting to take to heart that one not sin so as to cause the angels to mourn over him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:19: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in his Pekudin (Zohar, Naso 123a) that "his mourners" are the two hundred and forty-eight mitzvot that mourn over him - his words: "all the positive commandments that were destined to rest in his two hundred and forty-eight commandments, they all mourn over him; and the secret of the matter is 'I have seen his ways and will heal him,' etc., 'and to his mourners' - these are the two hundred and forty-eight commandments that mourn over him, for they are the supernal image resting on his head, in which YHVH rests" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:20: Further, concerning the blemish pertaining to the days, our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in Pesikta Rabbati - their words: "(Proverbs 4:23) 'above all that you guard, watch over your heart' - Rabbi Acha said, there are two hundred and forty-eight positive commandments in the Torah, corresponding to the two hundred and forty-eight limbs of a person, for every single limb cries out to the person, 'perform a mitzvah with me, so that you may live and lengthen your days by its merit'; and there are three hundred and sixty-five negative commandments, corresponding to the number of the sun's days, so that every day, from the hour the sun rises until it sets, it cries out and says to a person: I decree upon you, by the One whose days have reached you on this day, that you not commit a transgression through me, and not tip the scale for me and for the whole world to the side of guilt" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:21: Along these lines, Rashbi explains (Emor 92a) - his words: "Come and see, we learn: a fast is as effective for [neutralizing] a [bad] dream as fire for tow, and the essence of the fast must be on that very day, not on another day. Why? Because there is no day below that is not governed by another day above; and when he begins the fast for the dream, we learn that day is not passed until that decree is annulled, and if he postpones it to another day - behold, that is the dominion of another day, and one day does not enter into another day's [dominion]. In this manner, there is no day that is not appointed by a supernal day above it, and a person must guard against causing a blemish on that day, and not be blemished before the other days."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:22: We learn: an act below arouses an act above. If a person acts properly below, so is a force aroused properly above; if a person does an act of kindness in the world, kindness is aroused above, and it takes hold on that day and is crowned by it because of him; a person conducts himself with mercy below, mercy is aroused for that day, and it is crowned with mercy because of him, and that day stands by him to be his guardian at the time he needs it - in this manner, and the reverse of this. And above all, if a person commits an act of cruelty, it arouses cruelty on that day and blemishes it, and afterward that day stands against him with cruelty, to destroy him from the world - in the measure a person measures, so it is measured to him" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:23: Along these lines, this passage explains, Rashbi explains (Vayechi 224a), that this is what David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 139:16) "the days were fashioned" - that the days themselves have a formation and a being, in which the soul is clothed after its departure from the world, according to the deeds it performed in them - his words: "Rabbi Yehudah opened and said, (Isaiah 42:18) 'hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, to see' - 'hear, you deaf' - these are people who do not heed the words of the Torah and do not open their ears to hear the command of their Master; 'and the blind' - who do not gaze to know upon what they stand, since every single day a herald goes forth and calls, yet no one pays heed - for we are taught that a person's days, when they are created, on the day he comes into the world, they all stand in their being and go and fly through the world; they descend and warn a person each day individually, and when that day comes and warns him, and the person commits a sin before his Master on that day, that day ascends in shame and testifies, and stands alone outside. And we learn that after it stands alone, it waits until the person repents of it; if he merited, that day returns to its place; if he did not merit, that day descends and joins with that spirit outside and returns to its house and is arranged in the very image of that person, in order to do him harm, and dwells with him in the house - and there is one whose dwelling is for good, if he merited, and if not, its dwelling with him is for evil. Either way, those days are recorded and diminished, and do not enter into the count of those that remain. Woe to that person who diminishes his days before the Holy King, and does not leave for himself days above with which to be crowned in that world and to draw near with them before the Holy King.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:24: Come and see: when those days draw near before the Holy King, if this person, who departs the world, is meritorious, he ascends and enters into those days, and they are the glorious garments in which his soul is clothed - those being the days in which he merited and did not sin. Woe to one who diminishes his days above, for when they wish to clothe him in his days, those days that he blemished through his sins are missing from that garment, and he is clothed in a defective vessel; how much more so if they are many, and the person has nothing with which to be clothed in that world - then woe to him, woe to his soul, for they judge him in Gehinnom for those days, day for day, double for one - for when he leaves this world, he finds no days with which to clothe himself, and he has no garment with which to cover himself. Happy are the righteous, whose days are all stored away with the Holy King, and from them are made glorious garments to be clothed in in the World to Come" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:25: He says afterward that concerning this it is said (Genesis 24:1) "and Abraham was old, advanced [ba] in days" - meaning that he entered into and was clothed in all his days, which had been properly repaired.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:26: Here is explained the punishment for one who does not properly repair all his days: "they judge him in Gehinnom day for day, double for one." The reason is that all of a person's days together are one complete garment, the measure of a complete stature, in which a person repairs his soul to clothe it; and any blemish on a single day is a blemish to the whole garment, so that his garment is found torn.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:27: This is likewise explained in the Talmud (Chagigah 5b): it says there of Rav Idi, that he would travel for three months to study for one day and return to his home for three months, and Rabbi Yochanan expounded concerning him (Isaiah 58:2) "yet they seek Me day by day" - whoever occupies himself with Torah even one day a year is considered as though he occupied himself with it the whole year; and it says, likewise concerning the measure of punishment, as it is written (Numbers 14:34) "according to the number of the days in which you spied out the land" - did they sin for forty years? Did they not sin for only forty days? Rather, this teaches you that whoever commits a transgression even one day a year, Scripture considers it as though he transgressed the whole year - so far.
